# dte-sdk

> TypeScript SDK for Chilean electronic tax documents (DTE): build, stamp (TED), sign (XMLDSig) and envelope documents for the SII and talk to the SII web services (upload, status, acceptance/claims), with an English domain model, bilingual EN/ES JSDoc and RUT handling delegated to rut.ts.

The package has four entries, ES modules only, on Node ≥ 22.12 (`require()` loads them too): `dte-sdk` (documents, stamps, signatures, envelopes, books and the SII web services client over `fetch`; also runs on Bun and Deno and bundles for the browser), `dte-sdk/node` (`createNodeHttpsTransport`, `createDirectoryCapture`, `createDirectoryUploadArchive`, `createDirectoryFolioRegistry`), `dte-sdk/portal` (the SII portal, folios, the register, the MIPYME backup, the certification sets and the certification runner) and `dte-sdk/pdf` (printed samples; needs the optional peers `pdf-lib` and `bwip-js`). `DteError` and `isDteError` come from `dte-sdk` and recognize what every entry throws.

dte-sdk covers document types 33, 34, 39, 41, 43, 46, 52, 56 and 61. `createDocument` validates and normalizes input (RUTs via rut.ts, text sanitized, schema lengths enforced, totals computed with per-line rounding, VAT-included prices via `MntBruto`, withholding for purchase invoices, receipt defaults). `toSiiDocument`/`fromSiiDocument` map the English model (`totalAmount`, `issuer.businessName`) to the official SII tags (`MntTotal`, `RznSoc`) in schema order. `stampDocument` builds the exact `<DD>` string and signs it with the CAF private key (SHA1withRSA over ISO-8859-1 bytes). `signDocument` applies the enveloped XMLDSig signature (C14N 1.0, RSA-SHA1) the SII validates. `createEnvelope`/`signEnvelope` produce `EnvioDTE`/`EnvioBOLETA`. Certificates load from PKCS#12 or PEM; CAF files are parsed and checked for range and the 6-month expiry of invoice/note CAFs. Status codes from the SII web services are classified (`accepted`, `pending`, `rejected`, `queryError`). Errors are `DteError` with stable codes and no personal data in messages. All clock-dependent functions accept `{ now }`.

The SII web services client is `createSiiClient({ environment, certificate, companyRut })` plus free functions: `uploadEnvelope`/`uploadBook`/`uploadFolioConsumption` (DTEUpload multipart in ISO-8859-1, or the receipts REST API in production; the XML must open with a declaration naming ISO-8859-1; duplicates return the original TrackID), `queryUploadStatus`/`waitForUploadStatus`/`queryDocumentStatus`/`folioReceived`, and the acceptance/claim registry `registerClaim`/`listClaimEvents`/`queryTransferable`/`queryReceptionDate`/`receiverStatus`. Tokens are obtained and renewed automatically per environment, channel and certificate. Transport is injectable (`fetch` by default, `createNodeHttpsTransport` from `dte-sdk/node` with TLS verification on; `tls.ca` adds to Node's bundled roots), retries use exponential backoff and never re-send an upload or a claim after an SII answer (not even a partial one), and `capture`/`archive` ports record redacted HTTP exchanges and the bytes of every upload.

The SII books are `createPurchaseSalesBook` (IECV, `LibroCompraVenta`), `createGuideBook` (`LibroGuia`) and `createFolioConsumption` (RCOF, `ConsumoFolios`), each with `build*Xml`, `sign*`, `verify*Signature` and `toSii*`. All submission kinds of the schemas are covered, and the SDK computes the summaries from the lines; `summaryOnlyTotals` and `previousTotals` carry what cannot be derived. An explicit line total that differs from the SII formula is kept and reported in `totalMismatches`, and `strictTotals: true` throws `BOOK_TOTAL_MISMATCH` instead. `bookEntryFromDocument`, `guideEntryFromDocument` and `folioConsumptionEntryFromDocument` derive the lines from issued documents. The signed XML goes to `uploadBook` or `uploadFolioConsumption`. The RCV replaced the IECV in production from period 2017-08, the guide book is sent only on SII request, and the report is used in the receipts certification; the SII probably no longer requires it in production.

Certification (deterministic half, from `dte-sdk/portal`): `parseTestSetText` parses the SII test-set text into sets and cases; `planCertificationSets` gives what each set issues and the folios per type; `createFolioAllocator` hands out folios with the CAF that stamps them; `issueTestSet` issues the basic, exempt, guide and purchase sets through phase 1 with the `SET` reference (`CASO <id>`) and the field rules, written as the reference writes them (UTC issue day and UTC stamps with milliseconds, unit prices with six decimals, zero totals on the notes that correct a text); `issueSimulation` re-issues every case in one envelope; `createCertificationSalesBook`, `createCertificationPurchaseBook` and `createCertificationGuideBook` build and sign the books through phase 3, as total submissions or adjustments, with the lines and summaries the reference writes (the withheld VAT rate as 0.19, the common-use credit rounded per document). Nothing sends: the runner does.

Certification (portal half, from `dte-sdk/portal`): `runCertification` runs the HTML side in the field's order from a `CertificationStore` (`createMemoryCertificationStore`, `createDirectoryCertificationStore`; the state holds CAF private keys): the test sets, the books, the simulation, the exchange set answered on the exchange portal (`downloadExchangeSet`, `validateExchangeUser`, `uploadExchangeAnswers`, `confirmExchange`; the answers from `createExchangeAnswers`, signed and schema-valid), the printed samples uploaded to the samples portal when the `samples` option gives them (`readPrintedSamples` from `dte-sdk/pdf`; `readSamplesReview`, `createSamplesReview`, `uploadSample`, `submitSamplesReview`, `readSamplesDetail`), and the declaration of compliance, irreversible, only with `declareCompliance: true`; it stops with `exchange` (the set unavailable or the company not in the exchange), `printedSamples` (no samples given), `rejected` (the SII's reasons in the detail) or `compliance`. Each phase is a step over the dependencies and the state (`obtainTestSet`, `prepareFolios`, `sendTestSet`, `declareTestSets`, `waitForTestSetsApproval`, `runBooks`, `advanceToNextStage`, `sendSimulation`, `declareSimulation`, `waitForSimulationApproval`, `runExchange`, `uploadPrintedSamples`, `declareComplianceFinal`), with typed progress events through `onProgress`; beneath them the portal operations `downloadTestSet` (generates the set anew at the SII), `declareProgress` (every field in form order, the page read again to verify), `readProgress`, `advanceStage`, `listBookHistory` and `declareCompliance`. The two GWT portals speak GWT-RPC (`gwtBody`, `gwtAnswer`); their hashes are discovered on the way in with the pair known to work as the fallback. The run keeps to the reference in what the SII receives and in how it flows: the declaration carries today's Chile date, the uploads of the run retry only network failures (eight attempts) and take `STATUS` 99 as a failed send, a portal request waits 20 s, and `receiver`, `resolution` and the issuer's activity, commune and city have defaults (`DEFAULT_CERTIFICATION_RECEIVER`, `DEFAULT_CERTIFICATION_ISSUER`). The books phase starts over on every run (the period from the UTC month the set was read in, the approved books from the portal), resends as adjustments or in the next free period, and never stops on a portal read; with the three mandatory books sent the runner asks for the next stage and stops with the portal's sentence when it does not move (`runBooks` is `incomplete` only when a mandatory book could not be sent; `advanceToNextStage` returns `advanced`, `unchanged`, `failed` or `timedOut` and never throws for a portal answer). The simulation carries the local date of the process and UTC stamps to the second; the declaration of compliance counts as made when the last page no longer shows its form. The waits are the field's and `sleep` and `now` are injectable. None of it has been run against the portal yet.

Certification of receipts (from `dte-sdk/portal`), an application of its own with no runner, as pieces to chain: `downloadReceiptsTestSet` (the plain-text set), `parseReceiptsTestSet`, `issueReceiptsSet` (one receipt of type 39 per case to the final consumer, prices with VAT, the reference `SET` / `CASO-<n>`, the signed `EnvioBOLETA`), `sendReceiptsSet` (uploads the envelope, waits 20 s, reads its status, then sends the folio consumption report with the sequence number 100 plus the attempt, up to ten attempts; `sent` unless the envelope is rejected, `envelopeRejected`, or the report cannot be uploaded or is refused for lack of authorisation, `consumptionFailed`), `declareReceiptsTrackId`, then later `readReceiptsStatus` (`readyToDeclare` at `P90`, `declared` at `P91`) and `declareReceiptsCompliance` (irreversible; `provider` is mandatory; the representative is the owner of the session; `alreadyDeclared` and `notReady` are outcomes), and `verifyReceiptsAuthorization` (type 39 among the stamping types of a production client, and the receipts row of the certification progress page; never throws, a form not served is `queryFailed`). A receipt (39, 41) takes `receiptReferences` (`code`, `reason`, optional `documentType` and `folio`), never `references`: the receipts schema has its own `Referencia`, without a date. None of it has been run against the receipts portal yet.

Printed samples (Node only, from `dte-sdk/pdf`): `parsePrintableDocuments` turns any `EnvioDTE`, `EnvioBOLETA`, bare `SetDTE` or bare `DTE` XML into printable documents with each `TED` copied verbatim; `renderPrintedSample` draws one single-page PDF per the SII printed-samples manual (21.5 cm wide, 11 to 33 cm tall, red type box, acknowledgement box and `CEDIBLE` mark on the transferable copy of 33, 34, 43, 46 and sale guides, PDF417 stamp with the signed bytes and its legends); `renderTedBarcode` gives the stamp PNG alone; `renderPrintedSamples` batches envelopes in memory into the test and simulation sets with failures as data; `writePrintedSamples` and `findEnvelopeFiles` do the same over files (`SET-PRUEBAS`, `SET-SIMULACION`). `pdf-lib` and `bwip-js` load on first use.

The SII portal, from `dte-sdk/portal`, is `createPortalClient({ environment, certificate, companyRut })` plus free functions, on Node (client certificate over `https`; TLS 1.2, server verified). The certificate must be enabled as a login method at sii.cl, or the login throws `SII_PORTAL_CERT_NOT_ENABLED`. Session: `openPortalSession`, `closePortalSession`, or on demand; `sessionCache` and `lock` are ports for several replicas. Company data: `fetchCompanyResolution` (per environment), `fetchTaxpayerData`, `fetchIssuerProfile`, `queryCertificationSets`. Folios: `listStampableTypes`, `queryFolioQuota` (`MAX_AUTOR`, `FOLIOS_DISP`; stamps nothing), `requestCaf` (may grant less than asked; read `granted`), `listFolioRanges`, `annulFolios` (explicit scope required; `maxRanges` limits one call; irreversible; counts against the quota for six months), `listReobtainableRanges`, `reobtainCaf`. Composite flows return refusals as data: `requestCafExact`, `requestCafInBatches`, `reobtainFolios`. Refusals are `SII_PORTAL_REJECTED` with `details.rejection` and `portalRejectionMessage`. `createFolioRegistry`, `createMemoryFolioRegistry` and `createDirectoryFolioRegistry` track folios locally. The CAF XML holds a private key: treat it as a secret.

The purchase and sales register runs on the portal session: `listPeriodDocuments`, `fetchRegisterSummary`, `listPurchaseTypes`, `fetchPurchaseDocument`. Response codes are not looked at, so a refused month reads as empty; rows have typed fields, `null` when absent, and `raw`. Writes on a production client change the real register: `changePurchaseType`, `moveVatToCommonUse`, `moveVatToRecoverable` are one attempt each, confirmed only by the SII's `OK`; on `purchaseChangeNotConfirmed` the change may have applied, so read the document again before retrying, and VAT amounts are final amounts, not a delta. `downloadMipymeBackup` reads the XML from production whatever the client's environment, in pieces of at most 20 documents, newest first, in the result or through `onChunk`. A day that cannot be downloaded throws before any download. Known defect: a two-day range over 20 documents downloads only its first day, while `total` counts both.
